status: final: committed before any held-out pair was scored
question: Does a user model fit on a researcher's pairs from before T predict his choices after T better than giving the model his raw pairs or his documents? (PLAN 6.3, 12.2)
cutoff: 2025-04-01 (moved from 2026-03-01 by Ethan, 2026-11-14, when merging cross-posts left 33 held-out decisions from 5 documents, under the floor of 40 from 10)

data.note: the distractor gate may rebuild flagged distractors before E2; E2 scores the pair files as they stand after the gate

arms.m0_named: no history, told whose choices these are (contamination probe)
arms.m1_pairs: his history pairs in the prompt
arms.m1_docs: his documents from before T in the prompt
arms.selected: the user-model method WS A (Gio) designates; the public track does not choose or compare methods

scoring: a pair is right only if the model picks his option in both a/b orders
primary_rule: success if the selected arm's accuracy minus each of m1_pairs and m1_docs has a 90% document-clustered bootstrap interval above 0
secondary: contamination gap: m0_named minus m0, with its clustered interval; a gap whose interval is above 0 means the model knows his work and E2 gains are reported as an upper bound
selected arm accuracy by decision tag, author position and distractor source
selected arm accuracy without pairs the gate still flags
model: claude-sonnet-5-5 for every arm; claude-opus-5-5 as the gate judge
no_post_hoc: no pair, document or arm is dropped after held-out scoring starts; T does not move again
amended: 2026-11-14, before any held-out scoring of the selected arm: the method comes from WS A, not from select_method on this researcher's history (Ethan)
